doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Getting the NBC staff job and the rock and roll guitar boom
summary: After leaving Vaughn, a cellist recommended him for an NBC staff job on live television; rock and roll created demand for guitarists in New York.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well I didn’t move into New York, I just started doing gigs. When I left Vaughn’s band luckily I had made connections, unknowingly, with all the violin players that I worked with on the Camel show. And most of them were contractors. And the rock & roll thing was hitting in New York and they were hiring a lot of guitar players. And one of the cello players, Maurice Brown, told me, “hey they need a guitar player over at NBC, want to go up? He says “I’ll recommend you. So he did. And I got the job. I started the job the following Monday. And I played a whole year with her, five days a week, on network television, NBC staff.
These would be for live TV shows?
It was a live TV show. And then while you were doing that, other people knew you. Then the rock & roll thing started to hit with — every recording session had four guitar players.
